title: Roadmap Dependency Corridor: alignment windows, contingency lanes, and team readiness probes
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a lightweight, time-boxed 'Dependency Corridor' process to make cross-team roadmap dependencies observable and time-bounded across Eng/Design/Security/Infra. The corridor defines alignment windows, contingency lanes (fallback plans), readiness probes, and a lightweight escalation path that surfaces risks early, reduces late-stage blockers, and enables automated nudges into the Console sync fabric.
acceptance_criteria: Published corridor definition doc with examples for low/medium/high-risk dependencies
Template and checklist created for product/engineering to declare a dependency with required readiness probes
Automation rules in the roadmap tracker to tag issues entering the corridor and trigger reminders 6w/3w/1w before alignment window
Two pilot initiatives (runtime-1.22 rollout and console-2025.04 dashboard revamp) run through corridor successfully with documented outcomes
Escalation playbook validated with a simulated missed-dependency scenario and sign-off from Eng, Design, Security, Infra leads

notes: Trade-offs discussed: strict gating vs. lightweight corridor. Chosen approach aims to reduce false positives and preserve delivery velocity for PLG flows.
Future work: integrate corridor state into Console rollouts view and expose dependency heatmap in per-route dashboards.
Risks: adoption friction across teams; plan two "office hours" sessions during pilots to collect friction points and update templates.
Measurement plan: adoption = % of medium/high-risk roadmap items tagged; impact = reduction in cross-team late blockers measured over two cycles
